subject: MerchantX: Initial IR notification, SOC 2 evidence request and onboarding
messages:
From: Alice Park <alice@merchantx.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@merchantx.com>, security@merchantx.com
Date: Tue, 09 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MerchantX — suspicious auth attempts (initial notify)

Hi Karthik,

We detected a cluster of failed API key attempts against our integration with Redwood Inference between 01:30–01:45 UTC this morning. We’ve throttled traffic on our side and blocked the IPs, but need to understand if any of these attempts touched customer data or if the keys were scoped to non-sensitive routes.

Can you confirm whether Redwood observed any anomalous requests matching MerchantX API keys and, if so, whether there was any successful token exchange or data exfil? We are preparing an executive summary for our internal security team and would appreciate initial context within the next 3 hours.

I’ve attached a short alert export (merchantx_ir_notification.pdf) and included our security alias.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Park
Senior Security Ops, MerchantX
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Park <alice@merchantx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, security@merchantx.com
Date: Tue, 09 Oct 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MerchantX — suspicious auth attempts (initial notify)

Hi Alice — thanks for the heads-up and the export. I’ve kicked off a short triage:

- Marissa (security lead) is running a logs pull for MerchantX API key identifiers and will check for successful token exchanges.
- Jonas (infra) will confirm whether any egress to unknown destinations occurred from the serving fleet.
- I’ll check key-scoping and rate-limit logs and provide a timeline.

Initial ask: could you confirm the exact MerchantX key IDs or truncated forms (last 4 chars) so we can match quickly?

We’ll assemble an initial statement for your execs and share raw artifacts via the Drive link I’ll create. Expect the first update within ~2 hours.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Park <alice@merchantx.com>, security@merchantx.com
Date: Tue, 09 Oct 2028 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MerchantX — suspicious auth attempts (initial notify)

Karthik / Jonas — quick findings from the log pull:

- Matching identifiers: merchantx_live_3a4f, merchantx_test_7c21 (both show failed attempts).
- There were three successful calls using merchantx_test_7c21 to a non-sensitive health-check endpoint (200 OK). No user PII returned.
- No evidence of KV-store or long-form payload retrieval in the time window.

I uploaded an evidence index (redwood_socrun_evidence_index.xlsx) to 
https://drive.redwood.com/Shared/merchantx/IR/2028-10-09 — includes log slices, per-region timestamps, and sanitized request headers.

Next actions I recommend:
- Formalize a short incident timeline and root cause hypothesis (token exfil vs bruteforce).
- Provide MerchantX the SOC 2 SIG mapping for the auth controls referenced in the log slices.
- Offer a short postmortem draft and a plan for rotated keys + revocation window.

I’m available for a 20-min sync if MerchantX wants a walk-through of the artifacts.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
From: Alice Park <alice@merchantx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, security@merchantx.com
Date: Tue, 09 Oct 2028 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MerchantX — suspicious auth attempts (initial notify)

Marissa — this is helpful, thank you. A couple of follow-ups from our compliance team:

1) We need a SIG/CAIQ crosswalk that points to the specific evidence items in your Drive export (control IDs + file names). Our auditor wants to see where the auth controls map to the SIG questionnaire answers.
2) Please include any E2E timeline showing when keys were issued, rotated, or shadowed. If you have an internal postmortem draft, share under the same Drive folder and we’ll mark any redactions.

We’d like a 30-min walkthrough tomorrow (Wed) at 10:00am PT to review artifacts and requested SIG mapping. Can you confirm?

Alice
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Park <alice@merchantx.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Oct 2028 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: MerchantX — IR postmortem draft and SIG/CAIQ evidence mapping (drive link)

Alice / team — thanks for the sync earlier. Following our walkthrough, attached is the postmortem draft (ir_postmortem-draft.md) and a SIG/CAIQ crosswalk that points at the artifacts in the evidence index. Summary below: 

- Root cause: weakly scoped test key (merchantx_test_7c21) exposed in a transient CI log; attacker used it for automated calls to a health endpoint — no PII or model outputs with customer data were returned.
- Impact: limited to test environment; production keys remained unused and were not involved in any successful calls.
- Remediation: rotated all MerchantX test keys, revoked any active sessions created with those keys, added CI secrets scanning rule, and added stricter token scopes to the SDK.
- Evidence delivered: sanitized logs (per-region), key rotation audit, CI pipeline config change, and SIG/CAIQ mapping spreadsheet.

Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/Shared/merchantx/IR/2028-10-09
HubSpot record: HS-4592

If you need a redacted PDF for auditors, we can produce one by EOD Friday. I’ll follow up when finalized and mark the closed timeline.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
